approach: Add a `bug-evidence` default to defaults.toml whose first sentence tells the reader to list it only for bug, wrong-output, regression or slowdown work. Add `ensure_bug_evidence(reading, request_texts)` in reading.rs beside `ensure_changelog`, and call it from `build_reading` after `ensure_changelog` and before `validate()`. For a `change` reading that already has at least one criterion, it adds one content criterion (data-backed root-cause evidence) and one `bug-evidence` defaults_applied entry, once each. Trigger, tier 1: the reader listed `bug-evidence` without a whole-phrase negation in `how`. Trigger, tier 2: a bug word within two tokens of a fix word in the request text, the retried job's request text (`attempt.request`), or the reading title. `read_once` passes both request texts. The reader prompt set grows past 2,000 tokens, so `BudgetSet::Reader` in crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs is raised by an appended decision D166, which says plainly that it is the decided exception to the context-engineer.md §8 rule and that the reader stays above 95%.

decisions.choice: Add the criterion and defaults entry as a step in `build_reading` beside `ensure_changelog`, not as a refusal in `refusing_check`.
decisions.reason: Root cause: bug jobs were rejected at the final verdict because no criterion demanded data-backed root-cause evidence. A step guarantees the criterion with no model round trip and refuses nothing. That means no replay refusal rate, no new `step!` line and no new refusal_corpus case. It follows `ensure_changelog` (reading.rs:281-303): idempotent, capability-gated, run before `validate()`.

rejected.option: A `check_*` refusal in `refusing_check` for a bug reading lacking the criterion
rejected.why: It adds a refusal rule (replay share, a corpus case that must refuse) and sends the reader round again for a sentence Athena can write itself.

rejected.option: Rely on the reader prompt and the default alone
rejected.why: Prose-only; the `mechanism` default asks for enforcement by mechanism.

decisions.choice: Two-tier trigger, only when `capability == Some("change")` and `acceptance_criteria` is non-empty. Tier 1: a defaults_applied entry with id `bug-evidence` whose `how` contains no negation. Tier 2: `names_bug_work(text)` is true for the request text, the earlier attempt's request text, or the reading title. `build_reading` takes `request_texts: &[&str]`; `read_once` builds it as `[request.text]` plus `attempt.request` when `attempt` is `Some` (reading.rs:521, 642-651; `EarlierAttempt.request` at briefs.rs:1991).
decisions.reason: Finding 6: the earlier attempt's request is already in hand in `read_once`, so on a retry such as 'try again on <id>' tier 2 can see the retried job's own request. The limit the earlier plan stated was one the plan created. `class_of_work` is a closed list with no bug class (athena.toml:128-129), so a keyword fallback is needed. `names_bug_work` lowercases, replaces 'wrong output' with 'wrong-output', splits on whitespace and trims non-alphanumeric characters from each token's ends (inner hyphens stay). Bug tokens: bug, bugs, regression, regressions, slowdown, slowdowns, wrong-output. A `regression` token followed by test, tests or testing is skipped. Fix tokens: fix, fixes, fixed, fixing, repair, repairs, repaired, diagnose, investigate. It is true when a bug token and a fix token have at most two tokens between them, in either order. `bug-fix` and `bugfix` count alone. Compounds such as `bug-evidence` match nothing. Remaining limit, stated in the doc comment and §3.9: a chain of retries whose earlier request is itself 'try again on <id>' carries no bug word, so only tier 1 and the title cover it.

rejected.option: Pass only the current request text (earlier plan)
rejected.why: Finding 6: a retry of a bug job is the usual way bug work returns after a rejection, and the current text then holds no bug word.

rejected.option: Bare `has_phrase` on title, summary and request text
rejected.why: It treats `-` as a word break, so `bug` matches in `bug-evidence`, and it matches 'regression test' and 'slowdowns' in feature requests.

rejected.option: A fix-intent word anywhere in the text
rejected.why: It fires on 'Fix the docs for the bug report form' and 'Fix a typo in the regression section'; the two-token window rejects both.

rejected.option: Add a `bug` class to `[classes]` in athena.toml
rejected.why: A new class is a job of its own, changes governance, and bug work is also code or tests.

rejected.option: No fallback, tier 1 only
rejected.why: A reader that never lists the default would escape the mechanism, which is how earlier bug jobs lacked the criterion.

decisions.choice: Make the reader instruction the main control on tier 1: the default's first sentence reads 'Only for bug, wrong-output, regression or slowdown work: name the root cause from readable data.' (wording may be tightened to fit the budget but must keep 'Only for' and the four work kinds). The negation list is a backstop only and matches whole phrases: the lowercased `how` contains 'not applicable', 'does not apply', "doesn't apply", 'does not fit', 'not a bug' or 'not relevant', or some whitespace-split token trimmed of punctuation equals 'n/a'. A negated tier-1 entry suppresses tier 1 only; tier 2 still decides.
decisions.reason: Finding 9: scanning free text is ad hoc. The reader sees the first sentence (defaults.rs render) and the reader prompt asks for each default that applies (reader.md:17), so telling it the scope is the mechanism. The substring 'n/a' would match words such as 'in/a', so it becomes a whole-token compare, and 'does not fit' is added. Other wordings still pass; the doc comment and §3.9 say so.

rejected.option: Keep substring 'n/a' and the five-phrase list as the control
rejected.why: Finding 9: loose, and other wordings get through with nothing telling the reader the scope.

rejected.option: Trust every tier-1 listing with no backstop
rejected.why: A feature reading that lists the default as 'not a bug job' would get an unmeetable criterion.

decisions.choice: Run the step only on a reading that already has at least one acceptance criterion: `ensure_bug_evidence` returns early when `reading.acceptance_criteria.is_empty()`. The call stays between `ensure_changelog` (842) and `validate()` (843).
decisions.reason: Finding 7: the guard at reading.rs:844-845 refuses a capability reading with no criteria ('a reading needs at least one acceptance criterion'). A step that added a criterion first would turn that refusal into an accepted reading holding only the step's sentence. The early return keeps the guard in force and the order test simple.

rejected.option: Call the step after the line-844 guard
rejected.why: It works, but moves the call away from `ensure_changelog` and `validate()`, which the order test and the reading's criterion 2 describe.

decisions.choice: Idempotency and duplicates: add the defaults entry only if no entry has id `bug-evidence`. Skip the criterion only if some criterion text, lowercased, starts with the constant's lead phrase 'before any fix, the change states the root cause'. A reader-written standing-default criterion such as 'root-cause: the change description names the root cause' does not suppress it.
decisions.reason: The standing `root-cause` default (defaults.toml:77-78) leads readers to write a criterion that asks for no readable data and does not rule out estimate-labelled guesses, which is the gap that got bug jobs rejected. Suppressing the step's criterion on it would lock the gap in. The cost is one more planner demonstration (admission.rs:179-197), which is intended.

rejected.option: Skip when the reader's criterion contains 'root cause' plus 'data' or 'estimate'
rejected.why: A marker-word match is as loose as a substring check; a duplicate costs one demonstration, a skipped criterion costs a rejected job.

rejected.option: Skip both when the defaults entry exists
rejected.why: A reader that lists the default but writes no criterion would escape the mechanism.

decisions.choice: The criterion is `kind: content` with text: 'Before any fix, the change states the root cause, shows it from data the job can read (records, a code path or a failing case) and shows why the wrong output or metric change follows from it; a guess labelled as an estimate does not meet this.' It has no path, no 'only ... may change' wording and no producer-report wording.
decisions.reason: A content criterion is judged from the diff. `producer_evidence_phrase` (reading.rs:4068), `check_boundary_and_repo_files` and `limits_changed_files` do not fire on it, and `check_environment_reach` reads behavior criteria only. A test runs `refusing_check` on the built reading. A newcomer can tell what evidence is required (outcome-check).

rejected.option: A behavior criterion naming a command
rejected.why: No single command shows root-cause evidence in general, and a behavior criterion triggers `check_code_survey` and `check_environment_reach`.

decisions.reason: Findings 1-5: each of these five files is forced by a test or rule, not chosen. (1) lib.rs holds the only reader budget (athena.toml has only reader_usd, reader_timeout_s, model and effort keys). (2) run_pin_tests.rs:1625 pins 'of 2000'. (3) `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` fails unless the facts line equals the computed size. Finding 8: the raise does not discharge the 95% displacement rule (context-engineer.md:231-232), so the decision says it is an exception and the reader stays above 95%. This follows the `behavior-evidence` precedent (CHANGELOG.md:3035-3042), which was paid for the same way.

risks.risk: The fallback misses a bug request with no listed bug word (for example 'fix the crash') or fires on a feature request with a bug word and a fix word within two tokens (for example 'Fix the bug report form').
risks.mitigation: Tier 1 covers paraphrases because the reader sees the default's first sentence. Tier 2 needs a bug token within two tokens of a fix token, ignores compounds such as bug-evidence, and skips 'regression test(s)'. The docs and typo cases are in the negative table; limits are in the doc comment and §3.9.

risks.risk: A retry whose earlier request is itself a retry ('try again on <id>' of 'try again on <id>') carries no bug word in either text.
risks.mitigation: Tier 1 (the reader sees the default and the earlier attempt's summary) and the title still apply. The limit is stated in the doc comment and §3.9. A test pins the one-level retry that works.

risks.risk: A reader lists `bug-evidence` for non-bug work with a 'how' that the negation backstop does not recognise, and the criterion is added to a feature reading.
risks.mitigation: The default's first sentence says 'Only for bug, wrong-output, regression or slowdown work'. The backstop catches the listed whole phrases; any other wording is trusted. A test pins each negation form and the 'in/a' non-match.

risks.risk: The step's criterion hides the empty-criteria refusal.
risks.mitigation: `ensure_bug_evidence` returns early on empty criteria; `bug_evidence_empty_criteria_still_refused` pins the refusal.

risks.risk: The added criterion text trips an existing reading check and refuses the whole reading.
risks.mitigation: The criterion is content kind with no path, no 'only ... may change' phrase and no producer-report wording; `bug_evidence_added_text_trips_no_refusal_check` runs `refusing_check` on the built reading.

risks.risk: The decision-log edit breaks the append-only or entry-structure rules (a D25 edit, a wrong id, a missing Provenance bullet).
risks.mitigation: Append only after the last entry, Grep `^## D` to confirm the highest id first, use the D165 bullet shape, leave D25 unedited. Run `cargo test -p athena-core mirrors` and the refusal_corpus test.

risks.risk: The raised budget leaves the reader above 95% and leaves stale figures in docs no test reads.
risks.mitigation: D166 and §3.9 state the exception and the next-addition duty. Step 10 greps for '1997', '99.85' and 'of 2000' and fixes each reader figure; older 1,930 history stays.

risks.risk: The step guarantees the criterion exists, not that the producer meets it; the final verdict is still the verifier's judgement, and its rejection logic is out of scope.
risks.mitigation: The doc comment and §3.9 say so. The default requires readable data and says an estimate-labelled guess does not meet it, which gives the verifier an explicit test.

risks.risk: One more criterion means one more planner demonstration on every bug reading, including readings where the reader wrote its own root-cause criterion.
risks.mitigation: Intended (a standing-default criterion does not require readable data). Documented in §3.9.

demonstrations.observes: Grep for `bug-evidence` in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs shows the id constant and the entry. The test asserts that `build_reading`'s body contains `ensure_changelog(&mut reading)`, then `ensure_bug_evidence(&mut reading, request_texts)`, then `reading.validate()`, in that order, and that `ensure_bug_evidence`'s source returns early unless capability is `change` and when criteria are empty. demonstrations.method: Unit tests drive the real `Athena::build_reading` through a new helper with bug requests, and call the step directly over positive and negative tables. They cover both tiers, the negated tier-1 entry, the standing-default criterion, retry by earlier request, the empty-criteria guard, idempotency, and that the added text trips no `refusing_check` step.
demonstrations.observes: All `bug_evidence_*` tests pass. (a) A change reading built from request 'Fix the bug where the report shows the wrong output' has exactly one content criterion starting 'Before any fix, the change states the root cause' and exactly one `bug-evidence` entry; `refusing_check` on it is None. (b) Tier 2 positives: 'Fix the regression in the parser', 'Investigate the slowdown in queue drain', 'Fix wrong-output in the status line', 'Fix the regression and add a regression test', 'Bugfix for the parser crash'. Negatives, which get neither criterion nor entry: 'Add a regression test for the parser', 'Add bug-evidence default and enforce root-cause criterion on bug', 'Throughput review: flag median slowdowns and queue a request', 'Fix the docs for the bug report form', 'Fix a typo in the regression section of the README', 'Describe the demo in README.md', 'Add debug logging', a study-capability bug request, a declined reading. (c) Tier 1: a change reading with a keyword-free request whose defaults_applied lists `bug-evidence` gains the criterion and no second entry. A tier-1 reading whose only root-cause criterion is 'root-cause: the change description names the root cause' still gains the step's criterion. Entries whose `how` is 'not applicable: this is not a bug job', 'does not fit: feature work', or 'n/a' on a feature request gain no criterion; a `how` containing 'in/a' as a substring of a word does not count as negated. (d) Retry: the request texts are ['try again on 20261105-234147-88tw', 'Fix the regression in the parser'] with a neutral title; the reading gains the criterion. The same with an earlier request 'Add a footer' and a neutral title gains nothing. (e) A bug request whose reading has an empty criteria list is still refused by `build_reading` with 'needs at least one acceptance criterion'. (f) Calling the step twice leaves the reading equal.
demonstrations.fails_without: With no step, (a) finds zero root-cause criteria and zero entries. With bare `has_phrase` matching, the negative table fails on 'bug-evidence', 'regression test' and 'slowdowns'. With a fix word allowed anywhere, the docs and typo cases fail. If the reader-written root-cause criterion suppressed the step, the standing-default case in (c) finds no criterion. Without the whole-phrase negation check the negated cases gain a criterion. Without the earlier-request input, (d) finds nothing. Without the empty-criteria early return, (e) is accepted instead of refused. With a non-idempotent step, (f) finds duplicates. Without the capability gate, the study case gains the criterion.
